verdicts.quote: Users who hold the bot's use permission find an app named "Grok Bot" in the Lightning Experience App Launcher
Nothing from Salesforce records is sent to xAI except what the user typed in the conversation ... no field values from the Account or any other record.
Nothing from Salesforce records is sent to xAI except what the user typed in the conversation
Two assignable permission sets exist, one granting use of the chat and one granting administration, and the administration set alone does not allow chatting
User A's conversations and messages never appear in user B's history list or transcript, including when B ... has the admin permission set of the bot.
the platform forbids making an HTTP callout after saving records in the same transaction ("uncommitted work pending"), so saving and calling are separate steps in a fixed order.
The key never appears in any page, ... any usage-log entry, any error message, any Salesforce debug log of the bot's own code, any notification, or the bot's deployable source
verdicts.missing: Where the key is actually stored (Named/External Credential or protected custom setting) is not decided.

verdicts.quote: the platform's maximum for one callout or continuation is 120 seconds
verdicts.missing: Callouts per transaction, heap and CPU time limits are not named or numbered (only callout timeout, 10,000 DML rows and concurrent requests are).

verdicts.quote: makes no real call to xAI (the platform does not allow real callouts in tests, so tests use stand-ins).
nothing else (outbound-call registration, tabs, app, settings defaults) needs to be configured by hand.
if the bot held a Salesforce request open for each waiting call, Salesforce's cap on concurrent long-running requests per org ... would refuse more than that many.
verdicts.missing: The mechanism by which the page learns the reply arrived (platform event, polling, Continuation, LMS) is not chosen.

verdicts.quote: results in exactly one message and at most one reply
When Salesforce rejects the work because too many long-running requests are running in the org at once, the message is marked failed with a notice that the system is busy.
any HTTP status 500 to 599 ... Grok is temporarily unavailable; Any xAI HTTP 4xx ... change or shorten the message; Grok did not answer in time
With xAI answering HTTP 429, the message is marked failed with a notice ... retrying in a little while is appropriate. / The bot never retries a failed call to xAI by itself
the stored and displayed reply is followed by a notice that it was cut off at the length limit. / any message waiting longer than (response timeout + 30 seconds) is shown as failed with Retry
Each message in a transcript displays its sender (the user or Grok), its text, its time and ... whether it is waiting or failed / model, outcome, ... prompt tokens and completion tokens
Conversations whose last activity is older than the retention period are removed automatically, together with all their messages
verdicts.missing: What happens to a user's conversations when that Salesforce user is deactivated or removed.

verdicts.quote: A request to xAI never carries the user's name, username, email, Salesforce ID, or the org's ID / Nothing from Salesforce records is sent to xAI except what the user typed
With the history window at its default of 20 messages, in a conversation of 30 earlier messages the request carries the 20 most recent earlier messages plus the new one
a 4,001-character message is not sent; the user sees that the limit is 4,000 characters ... a 4,000-character message is accepted.
bot enabled = on; model = "grok-4" ... / A holder of the admin permission can open a list view of usage entries and build a report grouping by user, outcome and day
No field of any usage-log entry contains the text of a user's message or of a reply
verdicts.missing: The log records who and when with retention, but no durable audit of what was asked and answered exists (conversations are user-deletable).

verdicts.quote: Deploying the bot's source to a new Developer Edition, scratch or sandbox org needs only three manual steps ... Salesforce requires at least 75% overall coverage ... to deploy to a production org
the user sees the failure of C-51 at the configured timeout and not later than the timeout plus 10 seconds. / a waiting indicator is visible until the reply or a failure arrives.
an empty history list with a notice that no conversations exist yet / a waiting indicator / a visible "failed" marking and a Retry action / a notice specific to that condition
After a deploy, no standard object, page layout, profile or existing permission set differs from before, and a user without the bot's permissions sees no difference in their org.
